agent.problem: At least five of the nine choice cards are discovery questions with no basis for a reasoned pick in the earlier cards: card 2 asks the trumpets' purposes, cards 6 and 7 ask for the east and south camps, card 10 asks who will sound the trumpets, and card 12 asks for God's specific promise in battle. Even counting every other choice as informed, only four of nine are informed guesses, so discovery questions make up too much of the stop.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: Six of the nine choice cards are multiple choice, compared with only two true-or-false cards and one fill-in-the-blank card. Multiple choice therefore dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
